reviews.title: I paid for the year. Then they stopped answering.
reviews.text:
I paid for the annual plan in June, after a week of loving this app. That was the last good week.

Since then it has quietly gotten worse. My profile settings don't save: I delete something, restart the app, and it's back. The app rewrites fields I filled in myself, putting words in my profile I never wrote. The feedback form can't be submitted at all, there's no way to scroll down to the send button. And the subscription page inside the app shows a plan, a price and a renewal date that have nothing to do with what I'm actually paying.

I wrote to support three times: June 17, August 17, September 1. 
In June they answered in half an hour and fixed the problem, so I know they can. Since then, nothing. Almost three months of nothing.

An app about manifesting your dream life, run by people who won't answer the ones who paid for it.

Quitting the Stella manifestation app is notoriously difficult and has sparked significant consumer frustration. Multiple user reviews on platforms like Reddit and Instagram highlight deceptive billing practices, hidden paywalls, and a lack of clear cancellation options within the app itself.Merely deleting your account or removing the app from your phone will not stop the weekly $6.99 (roughly $28/month) charges.Why Users Struggle to QuitObscured Mechanisms: Users report that there is no functional, visible button to cancel a subscription directly inside the application interface.Aggressive Billing: The app frequently attempts multiple unauthorized card charges per day if a balance is low, immediately executing back-charges the moment funds become available.Deleted Feedback: Honest reviews or complaints about cancellation issues are systematically scrubbed or ignored on the developer's social media pages.How to Successfully Cancel and Stop ChargesBecause the app's internal settings cannot be relied upon, you must bypass it completely and cancel through your phone's native ecosystem or your bank.For Apple iOS UsersIf you downloaded the app via the App Store, Apple manages the billing:Open your iPhone Settings app.Tap your name / Apple ID at the top of the screen.Tap Subscriptions.Locate Stella (published under Perl Productions LLC or MWM).Tap Cancel Subscription. If you only see an expiration date in red, it is already cancelled.
You could have told me that I had to pay for it before I wrote all of that! Oh and also if you really know how to manifest SOooooo well than you wouldn’t need me to give you money!

reviews.title: AI-based, high subscription fees, and false advertising.
reviews.text:
Last week I discovered that the stories are generated entirely utilizing AI. The app was also built using AI. 

I find this marketing strategy to be incredibly deceptive. So many individuals have concerns over AI and it’s environmental impacts. Nowhere is it stated in the app catalog or the countless promotional videos it relies on AI.

I was really excited for this app at first I downloaded it and uninstalled it when I found out it was $6.99 a week resulting in $28 a month more than your standard streaming services. I want to say it’s $10 short of AppleOne family that includes AppleMusic, AppleTV, and Cloud storage for your family. It costs much more than a majority of streaming platforms. 

I then reinstalled it and started to use it. Stella routinely pronounced my name wrong no matter how many times I provided that feedback. It got to the point where I requested not to say my name in the stories — it didn’t listen. I broke down the pronunciation and it didn’t respond to that either. I don’t know how I’m supposed to be envisioning something as my future self when my name isn’t even pronounced correctly. 

Stella also misgendered me on a handful of occasions even though my gender/pronouns were in there. After stating my sexuality was queer, Stella originally only generated love stories for a heterosexual person. They were all generated with he/him pronouns. I put in a customization for that change. And what is the point of having options for your name if it’s going to be pronounced incorrectly, for reference my name in there is Andi. When I said it’s pronounced “and-i” please use that version, it pronounced my name incorrectly with then it explaining how he pronounced it just the way I like with literally saying “And I” rather than “Andi”. It was a major turnoff. 

I still continued to use the app in the beliefs it could be working. 

The stories though are like all the sudden I have this perfect life and I’m not saying it’s not possible. I’m saying it leaves no room for humanity. I started to find it a bit weird or hearing these stories like this isn’t me or the life I want. I mean what I wrote yes, the way it’s told, no. I felt like it landed me disconnected/ unrelatable to 90% of society. 

It was the AI-generated storytelling in comparison to price point and then absence of data privacy that resulted in my deletion of my account. 

Applications that have top of the line developers don’t even charge this much. Sarah, the founder, constantly talks about being a self-made millionaire while neglecting the fact that her services are significantly above average in costs. It’s one thing to be a self-made millionaire and it’s another to be taking advantage of your consumer. 

For an app that was primarily based in AI, a year long subscription is $361. My subscription to Headspace is $100 a year and the Chani app is $120-130 a year — neither of them use AI. 

I did use the application for a few weeks or a month. Then I discovered how it is entirely reliant on AI with completely false and deceptive marketing. 
They say not to tell your manifestations and dreams to everyone. Well on AI-generated applications such as this they go into a larger database and could be extracted for usage. There is no user privacy and they are your dreams. 

If you had an amazing business idea, business plan, or opportunity, it will be uploaded and stored in their cloud, software center to be accessed by anyone at a later day. Thus it can take your proprietary ideas as their own. 

The support page is a GitHub website. It’s not even a genuine support page. It returns you to a primary coding platform. 

At first I thought Stella was designed by software engineers and coders, I thought there was advanced coding language involved to generate the stories, such as how Siri or Alexa will talk to you. It is not. It is entirely generated via artificial intelligence. 

In short, your data isn’t safe on here, your dreams can be taken for someone else’s use. 

I’m most of all completely discouraged and disappointed by the fact that the extent of the AI-usage of this app is completely hidden and masked from the consumer.
